text:
alicia: heads-up — legal wants tenant ACME to be 'no-egress-outside-eu' for their private control plane. they also asked what happens if the eu pool is saturated. do we fail or fall back to a different model variant? :thinking:

sanjay: short answer: depends on contract. we have three behavior modes in runtime today: fail-closed, degrade-to-local-variant, and region-fallback. for private/VPC we can enforce 'fail-closed' at the network layer. but we can also implement a 'degrade-to-offline-quant' variant that never leaves the tenant region if we ship the model there.

marta: product preference — default for Enterprise+ should be fail-closed unless customer explicitly opts into degraded-mode. customers expect predictable data residency. however some customers want degraded-mode for availability guarantees. we need a clear opt-in UI.

ben: billing question — if we degrade to a cheaper local quantized model, how do we bill? also what about eval/quality telemetry?

sanjay: billing: tokens are billed against the model variant actually served. we already attach model_variant_id to usage events. add a new flag 'fallback_model_id' and 'fallback_reason' in telemetry. quality: emit a 'fallback_quality_check' event with sample prompts when fallback happens (if customer allows).

alicia: legal: you said contract language requires 'no egress outside allowed regions' — is degraded-mode allowed if the fallback stays inside region?

legal: short answer: yes if fallback remains inside the same approved regions and the contract includes 'allow_degraded_operation' checkbox. otherwise must be fail-closed. also need audit log entries for every fallback. :lock:

infra-bot: implementation idea: add tenant-level config fields on control plane: 
```
tenant_routing_policy:
  egress_allowed_regions: ["eu-west-1"]
  model_fallback_policy: "fail-closed" # options: fail-closed | allow-regional-variant | allow-local-quant
  allowed_fallback_variants: ["redwood-quant-8b-eu"]
  audit_log_endpoint: "https://log.ingest.redwood/private/tenants/ACME"
```
This enforces at the request router and is used by the runtime to select variants.

sanjay: we'll need the router to evaluate per-request: 1) tenant policy 2) model compatibility (latency, seq_len) 3) circuit-breaker state. fallback only when policy allows. default for private control plane = fail-closed.

marta: console UX: tenant settings page should surface these fields with tooltips: "Allowed regions", "Fallback policy" and a read-only list of allowed_fallback_variants. add a warning banner when policy is stricter than default. also expose telemetry dashboards: fallback rate, avg latency pre/post fallback, % of requests failed due to egress.

ben: requests for billing: add a meter tag 'served_variant' and update billing pipeline to prefer served_variant over requested_model for unit pricing. also ensure refunds if we fail-closed and customer has SLO credits.

alicia: SRE/runbook: what are operational alerts?

ops-bot: alert suggestions: 
- high_egress_violation_rate (> 0.1% over 5m)
- fallback_rate_spike (> 1% sustained 15m)
- model_variant_unavailable (per region)
Include playbook: if high fallback_rate and tenant policy = fail-closed, page oncall.

infra-bot: network enforcement notes: for onprem-private-controlplane we propose egress-proxies per-tenant and iptables rules at the envoy-egress: 
```
# example iptables snippet (pseudo)
iptables -A OUTPUT -m owner --uid-owner tenant-uid-123 -d 54.12.34.0/24 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -m owner --uid-owner tenant-uid-123 -j DROP
```
Combine with egress proxy for TLS termination and allowlist lookup.

marta: rollout plan: default to fail-closed for new private tenants. add a staged flag to allow-regional-variant for a small beta group. need migration script for existing tenants with ambiguous settings.

legal: action: update standard private deployment addendum with clause: "Customer may opt into degraded operation limited to approved regions only; all fallback events will be logged and exposed to Customer."

sanjay: API change items: 
- POST /tenants/{id}/routing-policy -> set egress_allowed_regions, model_fallback_policy, allowed_fallback_variants
- GET /tenants/{id}/routing-policy -> readonly for console
- Telemetry: emit events 'egress_blocked', 'fallback_used', 'fallback_allowed' with fields tenant_id, request_id, requested_model_id, served_model_id, reason, timestamp

alicia: security: also require KMS policy that keys never leave allowed regions for encrypted artifacts (models, kv cache). add KMS geo-tag in tenant config.

ben: final ask: make sure billing and console metrics match. i.e., "served_variant" must be first-class in BigQuery export.

marta: summarizing action items: 1) eng: implement router + iptables proxy enforcement (sanjay + infra) 2) eng: API + telemetry (sanjay) 3) product: console UX and migration (marta) 4) SRE: runbooks/alerts (ops) 5) legal: addendum update (legal). I'll open a RFC doc after this thread.

alicia: thanks everyone. I'll sync with ACME legal tomorrow and capture their exact checkbox choices. cc @ops-bot @infra-bot :thumbsup:
